To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new analytical framework for evaluating the joint detection performance of two sensors in a wireless sensor network scenario, where sensors do not perform any data compression, and we have derived an optimal coding scheme for this scenario that allows to approach the Slepian Wolf performance in AWGN channels and to outperform it over Rayleigh fading channels.

the proposed coding and iterative decoding scheme allows to exploit the correlation of sources in a wireless sensor network scenario, and to approach the ideal performance of the Slepian- Wolf scheme.

1) the use of recursive convolutional codes allows a noticeable performance gain in terms of packet error rate with respect to non recursive coding schemes; 2) the use of joint iterative decoding allows to approach the Slepian Wolf theoretical bound; 3) recursive convolutional coding and joint iterative decoding allow to outperform the Slepian wolf theoretical bound over fading channels, thanks to correlation diversity gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of optimal convolutional coding schemes for joint decoding of distributed correlated sources in wireless networks.
a novel approach for joint decoding of sources, which is based on a novel analytical framework and on the design of optimal convolutional coding schemes.

the design of low complexity coding schemes for wireless sensor networks, which are able to exploit the correlation of the transmitted sources in order to achieve performance close to the ideal Slepain-Wolf scheme, and to outperform it in fading channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the context of wireless sensor networks, the proposed joint decoding scheme with recursive codes allows to achieve a good trade-off between complexity and performance, and to approach Slepian-Wolfs performance.
the proposed scheme, which is based on the design of convolutional codes, allows a significant performance gain in terms of both complexity and achievable rates.

the joint decoding scheme proposed in this work, which is based on a low-complexity recursive convolutional coding scheme, allows a noticeable performance improvement with respect to the Slepian Wolf scheme, both in terms of achievable data rates and in terms of robustness against fading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a joint decoding scheme for correlated sources in wireless sensors network, which is based on low complexity convolutional codes and iterative decoding.
the proposed scheme allows for a low complexity solution for the joint detection problem in correlated wireless sensor networks, and that it can be applied in a wide range of scenarios.
, by using the proposed scheme, the two sensor nodes can achieve an error probability close to the Slepian Wolf limit, with a complexity that is only slightly higher than that of the uncoded scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in a wireless sensor network scenario, it is not always necessary to perform compression of sensed data at the source, but it is sufficient to exploit the correlation between sources at the destination.

, in wireless sensor networks, joint decoding of correlated information can outperform Slepian-Wolff coding with negligible complexity increase at the decoder, and with negligible increase in bandwidth and delay.
the proposed joint decoding scheme can be used in a variety of applications where the sensing nodes are not able to pre-compress the sensed data.
